newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran encourages foreign investment in electricity.
newsitem.headline: Iran encourages foreign investment in electricity.

text.p: Iranian acting energy minister Majid Qasemi said Iran is encouraging foreign investment to meet the capital cost of building power plants to meet the country's growing electricity demand, the Iran News reported on Monday.

"Qasemi told the English language daily Iran news that the build-operate-transfer method is considered a positive procedure towards the production of energy," the official Iranian news agency IRNA reported.
Electricity consumption had risen to 16,000-megawatts (MW) from 7,800 MW in 1989 and would increase to 20,000 MW at the end of the country's second five year plan (1995-2000).
Per capita electricity consumption currently stood at 1,388 kilowatt hours a year and would rise to 1,750 kilowatts hour a year at the end of the plan.
Foreign exchange shortages prompted the country's oil ministry last year to offer foreign investors contracts to develop Iran's oil and gas industry.
